parameters.meaning: kill probability of weapon i against target j
kill-probability threshold required for target j to be considered destroyed

variables.meaning: 1 if weapon i is assigned to target j; 0 otherwise
1 if target j is considered destroyed; 0 otherwise

derived.meaning: survival probability of target j under assigned weapons

derived.formula: y_j * max(0, K_j(X)-k_j), equivalently y_j*((1-k_j)-S_j(X)) under the destruction-linking constraint
derived.meaning: overkill penalty for destroyed target j
invalid-kill penalty: weapons assigned to an undestroyed target

objective.formula: sum_j v_j*y_j - sum_j OV_j(X,Y) - sum_j IK_j(X,Y)
objective.meaning: maximize destroyed-target value while penalizing overkill and invalid kill

constraints.formula: sum_j x_ij <= 1 for all weapons i
constraints.meaning: each weapon is assigned to at most one target

constraints.formula: S_j(X) <= 1 - k_j*y_j for all targets j
constraints.meaning: target j can be declared destroyed only if its kill threshold is reached

equivalence_rules: The nonlinear survival product may be log-transformed or linearized for a solver if the transformed model remains equivalent.
The overkill penalty can be represented using survival probability or kill probability, provided it penalizes excess above threshold only for destroyed targets.
A model that only maximizes destroyed value without invalid-kill and overkill penalties is not equivalent.
algorithm_boundary: logarithmic transformation, TSHHS, SimpleO and MMRBH are solution algorithms; they are not the gold optimization model
public_private_boundary: All planted assignments, destruction schemes, sampled stochastic outcomes, objective values and algorithm traces are private validation only.
